signals.name: Micron
signals.label: Whale conviction fracturing even as Congress keeps buying
signals.detail: Soros added 7.9x (2,824 -> 22,422 sh, ~$25.9M) in Q2-2026, but Tepper cut his Micron stake 41% and Druckenmiller dumped it entirely the same quarter. Congress has been unusually active: 8 purchases vs 3 sales in the past 6 months (Reps. Newhouse, Rulli, Gottheimer, Sen. Whitehouse among buyers), some sitting on gains as high as +229% since Feb 2026 buys.
signals.takeaway: Chip-memory conviction is fracturing among whales (Soros in, Tepper/Druckenmiller out) even as Congress keeps buying — a name to watch for a re-convergence next quarter rather than a clean consensus signal today.

signals.name: Nvidia
signals.label: Sharpest whale divergence of the Q2-2026 cycle
signals.detail: Tepper added (+53,500 sh to 1,525,000, ~$305M); Dan Loeb (Third Point) exited 100% (sold all 190,000 sh); Soros bought NVDA puts (bearish overlay); Burry's SOXX short (~9% NVDA-weighted, via Substack, no longer 13F-reportable) is reportedly working after SOXX fell ~21% in July.
signals.takeaway: Three schools of smart money took three different sides on the same stock in the same quarter — treat as a volatility/conviction-dispersion flag rather than a directional signal, and note it sits directly upstream of the Aug 19-20 AI-valuation unwind that hit KOSPI and US tech.

signals.name: Warner Bros. Discovery
signals.label: Triple-whale convergence, post-merger-approval
signals.detail: Loeb (Third Point) opened a new $533.2M/20M-share stake; Einhorn (Greenlight) opened a new $59.9M/2.25M-share stake; Soros added to reach $39.7M/1,488,690 shares — all in Q2-2026, right after WBD shareholders approved the Paramount Skydance merger (23 Apr 2026).
signals.takeaway: An unusual cross-style alignment (activist/value/macro) on a single post-merger media name — worth its own watch card rather than folding into the AI-mega-cap noise.

signals.name: Alphabet
signals.label: Still the broadest whale magnet, but Ackman just exited
signals.detail: Berkshire added 48,144,587 shares (+$21.1B, SEC EDGAR primary) and Loeb quadrupled his stake to 1,025,000 shares in Q2-2026 — but Pershing Square (Ackman) fully exited Alphabet the same quarter to help fund a Microsoft/Meta add.
signals.takeaway: Near-unanimous whale conviction now has a genuine crack; still the most broadly held AI mega-cap, but no longer unanimous.

signals.name: Taiwan Semiconductor
signals.label: Congress + fresh whale buy
signals.detail: Congress: 39 purchases over the past year totaling >$1.297M, a consistently top-purchased name (Quiver). Whale: Soros opened a new TSM position in Q2-2026.
signals.takeaway: Durable multi-quarter congressional buying now reinforced by a fresh macro-fund entry — the cleanest picks-and-shovels AI-foundry overlap this run.

signals.name: Silver
signals.label: A real breakout this time, driven by a Treasury buyback surprise
signals.detail: Silver ETF +4.47% Wed 19 Aug then +2.75% Thu 20 Aug (silver futures +2.80%/+4.38%) after the US Treasury doubled its long-bond buyback size, pulling real yields and the dollar down; miners led with GDX +9.42%/+2.59% and SILJ +9.55%/+0.67% the two sessions. 6th consecutive annual structural silver deficit underpins the move (Silver Institute/Metals Focus).
signals.takeaway: Unlike the false Monday-17-Aug 'breakout' (a futures-roll artifact, corrected in the prior brief), this move is confirmed across GLD/SLV/GDX/SILJ and grounded in a real catalyst (the buyback) plus the structural deficit — favor holding through near-term equity-risk-off given miners decelerated but did not reverse on Thursday's VIX spike.

signals.name: Energy Fuels
signals.label: Bridgewater opened a new stake same quarter management bought on the open market
signals.detail: Bridgewater Associates took a new $2.3M/160,899-share position in Q2-2026 (SEC EDGAR), layering onto the CEO/director open-market buys ($12.70-13.08, 7-8 Jul) already on record; UUUU fell -6.40% Thu 20 Aug in the broad AI-fear-driven rare-earth risk-off, unrelated to any company-specific news.
signals.takeaway: A rare case of a macro whale and insiders both accumulating the same rare-earth name; Thursday's drop looks like sector-wide de-risking rather than a fundamental reassessment.

superInvestors.name: Berkshire Hathaway / Greg Abel
superInvestors.rationale: Berkshire's largest single Q2-2026 move: a further $21.1B add to Alphabet, alongside a $1.64B add to Delta Air Lines (+17,510,544 sh). Filed to SEC EDGAR 14 Aug 2026.
superInvestors.deepDive: Extends the Q1 near-tripling of the GOOGL stake into a second consecutive quarter of aggressive accumulation under Abel — the single largest and most consistent whale conviction bet in the entire tracked cohort.

superInvestors.name: Soros Fund Management
superInvestors.rationale: Soros increased its Micron stake nearly eightfold; also opened a new Warner Bros. Discovery stake (+396,080 sh to 1,488,690, ~$39.7M), bought NVDA puts (bearish options overlay), and fully exited Fluor (FLR) — the opposite of Druckenmiller, who opened a new FLR position the same quarter. Filed 14 Aug 2026.
superInvestors.deepDive: A genuinely two-sided book this quarter: aggressive memory-chip accumulation and a media-conglomerate entry, hedged by a bearish NVDA options position — consistent with the fund's history of pairing directional adds with tail hedges.

superInvestors.name: Pershing Square / Bill Ackman
superInvestors.value: funded a Microsoft (+9.8%, $2.32B) and Meta (+20.1%, $1.80B) add

superInvestors.deepDive: The single biggest crack in this quarter's near-unanimous Alphabet whale conviction — a genuine rotation away from the name Berkshire just added $21.1B to, in the same reporting window.

superInvestors.name: Appaloosa / David Tepper
superInvestors.rationale: Tepper added to Nvidia while cutting his Micron share count 41% and adding to Meta (+$130M) and Alphabet (+$157M). Filed 14 Aug 2026.

superInvestors.name: Third Point / Dan Loeb
